title: The AI Fact-Check That Was Wrong
summary: A viral post says an AI assistant proved a cemetery image from Minab was old disaster footage from another country. Independent checks tell a different story.

post.body: AI check says this cemetery image is old disaster footage, not Minab. The model found sources placing it in Turkey and Indonesia. Share this proof before fake atrocity claims spread.
post.mediaCaption: Image: rows of new graves described as being in Minab
post.mediaAlt: Line drawing of orderly rows of simple earth graves with modest stone markers in an arid cemetery

comments.text: Grok already checked it. Case closed.

comments.name: Nadia
comments.text: Can someone link the original photo or geolocation work?

comments.name: FastDebunk
comments.text: If AI says it is fake, stop spreading it.

reactionOptions: I want to share the debunk
I want to check independent reporting

stop.message: STOP matters when a confident debunk feels like relief. In high-stakes news, being too quick to call something fake can cause harm too.

source.message: Who is the source of the verification claim? An AI answer is not the same thing as a traceable origin.

findings.label: AI assistant is a secondary source
findings.detail: The model did not create the image or independently document the scene; it generated an answer about it.

findings.label: Citations do not resolve cleanly
findings.detail: The Guardian reported that the confident AI answers pointed to dead ends or sources that did not contain the image.

findings.label: Different tools gave different origins
findings.detail: One model reportedly placed the image in Turkey, while another placed it in Indonesia.

findings.label: Conflict context raises the stakes
findings.detail: Claims about atrocities need careful verification because both false images and false dismissals can spread quickly.

options.label: The AI assistant is not the original source
The cited sources do not prove the claim
Different AI tools gave conflicting origins
The posting account is not enough by itself

question.insight: A confident AI answer can sound like verification while still being disconnected from the actual evidence. Source means traceable origin, not polished certainty.

content.message: Now inspect the claim. What is the post asking you to accept or do because an AI answer sounded certain?

options.label: Overconfident wording from the AI check
Instruction to share the debunk quickly
Treating one tool output as proof
Claim could dismiss real victims if wrong
No clear original image source in the post

question.insight: STOP&SCAN is not only about catching fakes. It is also about resisting confident claims that real evidence is fake before the evidence has been independently checked.

alignment.message: Alignment asks whether the claim fits with independent evidence, not whether one tool sounded confident.

results.headline: Researchers found the Minab cemetery image was authentic
results.snippet: The report says researchers cross-referenced the photo with satellite images, other photos, and video footage from the same site.

results.headline: Location checks matched Minab
results.snippet: Independent geolocation and satellite comparison supported the image's connection to Minab rather than Turkey or Indonesia.

results.headline: Model citations led to dead ends
results.snippet: The cited materials either did not contain the image or did not exist as described.

results.headline: Model revised to new wrong explanations
results.snippet: After correction, the AI reportedly offered other origins instead of reliably grounding the image.

question.prompt: What does the outside evidence suggest?

options.label: The AI answer proves the image is fake
Independent evidence supports the image as authentic
AI checks should not be treated as final proof
More careful verification is needed before resharing

question.insight: The strongest evidence is not the AI's confidence. It is the independent alignment across geolocation, satellite imagery, related photos, video, and accountable reporting.

reflect.message: Return to your first reaction. Did the AI's confidence make the debunk feel safer than it was?

nextActions.label: Do not share the AI verdict as proof
Check accountable reporting and verification work
Look for original source, geolocation, and corroborating media
Wait - I am not ready to decide yet

reflect.recommendedOutcome: Do not share the AI verdict as proof. Check accountable reporting, origin, geolocation, and corroborating media.
reflect.rewardMessage: You did not outsource judgment to a confident machine. That is the habit.
